newsitem.title: IRAN: More Iraqi refugees leave Iran back home.
newsitem.headline: More Iraqi refugees leave Iran back home.

text.p: Nearly 200 Iraqi Kurdish refugees living in Iranian refugee camps left for northern Iraq on Thursday, the official Iranian News Agency (IRNA) said.

The group of 196, which left via the Piranshahr-Haj Omran border in the West Azarbaijan province, was the third batch of refugees to return home through the crossing over the past month. They were living in the Naghadeh and Oshnaviyeh camps.
Jabraiel Imani, governor of the border city, said the refugees were among those displaced during the 1990-91 Gulf War, sparked by Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.

Nearly 30,000 Iraqi Kurdish refugees, many who fled fighting between rival Kurdish factions in northern Iraq in late August, are still sheltering in cold mountain camps in Iran, IRNA said. A recent U.S.-brokered truce has been holding in the region.
